STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole green pear on a white plate, photographed from directly above. There are a few small carrot shreds and crumbs on the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is square-ish, about 25 cm across at its widest, so its area is roughly 500 cm² (a square-ish plate is a bit less than a circle of the same width, so call it about 480 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: One whole pear. Tiny carrot shreds, which are leftover bits and negligible.

STEP 4 - Area: The pear is about 130 px wide against a plate about 345 px wide, so it is roughly 9.5 cm wide and about 9.5 cm long. Its area is about 3.14 × 4.75² ≈ 70 cm², or about 14% of the plate. The carrot shreds cover about 0.3%.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pear is roughly a sphere or ellipsoid about 9 cm tall. An ellipsoid of 9.5 × 9.5 × 8 cm has a volume of about 0.52 × 9.5 × 9.5 × 8 ≈ 375 ml. The pear looks smaller than that, and the plate may be a little smaller than I estimated, so I will use about 300 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Pear density is about 0.6 to 0.95 g/ml for a whole fruit. At 0.62 that gives about 185 g. A pear this size typically weighs 180 to 200 g, so I will use 185 g. The carrot shreds add about 1 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Pear is about 57 kcal/100 g, so 185 g is about 105 kcal. Carrot is about 41 kcal/100 g, so 1 g is about 0.4 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium pear of about 185 g and about 105 kcal is plausible.
